questions.question: What is the core invariant of an advanced observability system?
options: Preserve context that connects a user outcome to its request path, service, operation, and change
Put every identifier on every metric
questions.explanation: Connected identity and context make evidence explainable. Volume alone does not establish which service, request, or release produced an outcome.

questions.question: A 10-minute window contains 100 failed traces. What does a 10% head probability retain in expectation?
options: Exactly 10 traces in every observed window
questions.explanation: A uniform 10% head decision retains 10 failures in expectation. A particular probabilistic window can retain more or fewer.

questions.question: Why can a head sampler not guarantee retention of every slow or failed request?
options: The root decision happens before the request's final duration and status are known
Parent-based sampling discards all child spans
Logs are required before a span can start
questions.explanation: Head sampling uses information available when the root span starts. Final latency and result belong to the completed request.

questions.question: A worker span is disconnected from the request that enqueued its job. Which change repairs that evidence path?
options: Propagate trace context in message metadata and create the appropriate consumer relationship or link
Retain the disconnected trace for another month
Put the job ID on a high-cardinality metric label
questions.explanation: The asynchronous boundary needs explicit context propagation and a modeled span relationship. Storage and presentation cannot recreate a missing link.

questions.question: Which OpenTelemetry log fields provide direct request correlation?
questions.explanation: The logs data model defines TraceId and SpanId so a log emitted during request processing can identify its trace and operation.

questions.question: Why should user IDs and order IDs usually stay out of metric attributes?
options: Their unbounded values can create excessive metric cardinality
Trace context already contains the user's identity
questions.explanation: Each distinct attribute set can create a separate metric stream. Unbounded business identifiers belong in controlled traces or logs, not metric dimensions.

questions.question: What should an automated root-cause suggestion be treated as?
options: A hypothesis backed by inspectable evidence and explicit uncertainty
A reason to auto-remediate every production incident
questions.explanation: Correlation and anomaly ranking can guide investigation, but causality still needs evidence, limits, and operator verification.
